assessments.reasoning: Section 4.1 begins on printed p. 301 with the proposal to add an output status argument. Printed p. 302 explains status bindings for goal success and failure and adds error as a third reported outcome. The surrounding metacall succeeds in these three cases.

challenge.method: Compared the earlier one-argument call, the two-argument status list, a goal that emits output before failing, and section 5.1's separate three-argument form on printed p. 303.
challenge.results: The proposal permits prior output to remain available when a goal ultimately fails and records the failure in the status. Run-time error also produces a status while the wrapper succeeds. The separate third control argument and stopped status do not belong to this two-argument proposal.

limitations: The statement covers the three reported outcomes in the proposed 1984 two-argument metacall. The publication does not establish implementation coverage or the behavior of a nonterminating goal.
